caveats: A Table A-1 row is an instruction NAME, not an encoding and not a semantic variant.
Probe acceptance is DECODE ACCEPTANCE ONLY, never semantic correctness.
A row counted as having an accepted encoding may be implemented on fewer units or operand forms than the manual documents; no per-unit denominator was produced.
The compact accepted total is not quoted as coverage: it moves with the probe register profiles. The not-implemented count does not.
No percentage of "the ISA" is defensible from these numbers and none is given.

verification.reasoning: Upheld and STRENGTHENED - the one row I could verify by execution rather than by reading. I re-ran the checker against the committed artifacts and it reproduces exactly in 1.1 s: four blocks, input_matches true for each, both output planes true for each, wav_sha256 1f276d81...ade37a3a, trace_sha256 3bb564c9, verified_connected_stops 16, passed true, exit 0. Non-circularity of the expected values confirmed by reading pcm_evidence.py lines 44-60: expected = struct.pack('<588f', *(x/32768 for x in channels[channel::2])) derived from wave.open on an external WAV the emulator did not produce. Note the track's own scope_not_covered says it 'did not re-run any recorded replay ... so I verified recorded artifacts rather than reproducibility' - but this reproducibility check was available from committed files all along and was not run. Three scope corrections. (a) The row merges two different a6 values: a6 == 1176 is asserted on the KERNEL event at pc 0xc003c398, while pending['a6'] at the entry event 0xc003c698 is the BLOCK INDEX, used as expected_offset = pending['a6'] * 588 * 4. Quoting 'b4==0, b6==2, a6==1176' as one scope tuple conflates them. (b) All four blocks write to the SAME output addresses 0x11800200 and 0x11800fc8 - four sequential unpacks into one double-buffer, not four distinct destination regions; input addresses step 0x930 (0x118381e0, 0x11838b10, 0x11839440, 0x11839d70). (c) The byte-equality check cannot discriminate rounding mode: x/32768 is a power-of-two scale, so for any 16-bit x the result is exactly representable in float32 and no rounding occurs. Byte equality proves the scale and the integer-to-float path but is insensitive to the rounding semantics an INTSP/MPYSP-based kernel would exercise.

verification.reasoning: Verified in full. tests/cstub/c674x-loop.c:10 carries the comment 'Frozen linear scheduler oracle: compare ordering, rejection and state across every supported II and body length, including predicate epilogs.' reference_issue() is an in-test re-implementation of the scheduling rule carrying one SPRUFE8B 7.13.1 citation for the interrupt-epilog rule on predicate loops ('Predicate loops are normally unbounded. Interrupt detection turns their current launch count into a finite epilog schedule, just as it does for SPLOOP/SPLOOPD'). compare_schedulers()'s nested loops are 16 II x 49 lengths x 4 modes x 4 iterations x 13 cycle values x 2 filters = 326,144 exactly, so PERFORMANCE.md:66's count is accurate to the unit - a rare case where a committed performance doc's number checks out precisely. The row's conclusion (equivalence to prior behaviour, cannot catch a shared misreading of the manual) is correct. The row's open question stays open: the comment says 'frozen', implying transcription from the prior implementation, but nothing in the file settles whether it was hand-derived from SPRUFE8B 7.13 instead.

verification.reasoning: The counts are correct. I rebuilt and re-ran the track's crprobe.c against the current tree and reproduced its table exactly: accepts are crlo 0,1,2,4,5,6,7,13,14,18,19,20,21,26,27 for read (15) and 0-7,13,14,18-21,26,27 for write (16); ICR read rejects; 13 acronyms reject both ways. Table 3-27 (printed page 378, PDF 378) does enumerate 30 acronyms over 28 distinct crlo encodings, so the denominator is defensible. control_read()'s `default: return 0` is genuinely unreachable — there is exactly one call site (cdj_c674x.c:2289) and it is gated by control_read_supported. THREE PROBLEMS. (1) The cited test name does not exist: `grep -n 'def test_' tests/test_c674x.py` has no `test_c674x_interrupt_and_control_registers`; the cstub block is compiled by `test_c674x_packets_and_branch_delays` (tests/test_c674x.py:145). (2) crprobe.c contains NO assertions — it prints what the emulator does and exits 0 — so grading its `expected_values` as 'independent-of-emulator' is a category error; its *encodings* are TI-form (I checked 0x028003E2 / 0x001003A2 field-by-field against the Figure on printed page 376 and against the TI-assembler words in analysis/dsp/isa_probe.json), but there are no expected values. It also lives only in the session scratchpad. (3) OMITTED VARIANT inside the row's own 'complete control register file' scope: Table 3-27 lists non-zero crhi encodings for ten acronyms (CSR crhi=00001, IFR crhi=00010, PCE1 crhi=10000, and the `0xxxx` wildcard rows for AMR, CSR, ICR, IER, IRP, ISR, ISTP, NRP). I probed eight of them and every one is rejected as 'instruction not implemented' because the decoder requires crhi==0 ((w & 0xffe)==0x3e2/0x3a2 && a==0, where a=(w>>13)&31). The track excluded crhi aliases from the denominator but never recorded that the documented alias encodings fail closed. Confidence should be medium, not high.

verification.reasoning: The masking half is verified: Table 2-7 (printed pages 36-37) makes bits 31-26 reserved, the MVC entry's NOTE on printed page 377 says 'The six MSBs of the AMR are reserved and therefore are not written to', and the probe shows 0xa5a5a5a5 stored as 0x01a5a5a5 (= & 0x03ffffff). The LATENCY half is misdescribed. The only thing SPRUFE8B documents here is the AMR *use stall* in section 7.15.2 (printed page 700): 'The AMR use stall where an instruction uses an address register in the cycle immediately following a write to the addressing mode register (AMR)' — a 1-cycle CPU stall after which execution continues normally. The emulator does not stall; it hard-faults. cdj_c674x.c:1629-1630 and :1691-1692 return stop(..., "AMR use interlock not implemented"), and address_width() at :240 returns false for the same window with the same message at :1636 and :1700. So a legal firmware sequence (MVC B1,AMR followed immediately by a load through A4-A7/B4-B7) stops the core rather than stalling one cycle. MVC itself has Delay Slots 0 (printed page 377), so there is no 'documented access latency' for the register value. Implementation is partial, not supported.

verification.reasoning: Most of the row verifies. Figure 2-4 (printed page 38) marks PWRD, PCC, DCC and PGIE as R/SW, so the non-storage of PWRD/PCC/DCC is a real R/SW round-trip violation; Table 2-9 confirms '14h C674x CPU' for CPUID; the emulator does write PGIE (value & 3) and keeps ITSR.GIE in step. BUT the SAT sub-claim is NOT established by the cited pages, and the committed test pins the emulator's own choice. The code at cdj_c674x.c:2404-2407 computes (old & 0xffff0100) | (old & value & 0x200) | (value & 3) — i.e. SAT_new = SAT_old AND SAT_written: write 0 clears, write 1 PRESERVES. Figure 2-4's legend (the only definition of WC anywhere in SPRUFE8B — one hit for 'cleared on write') reads 'WC = Bit is cleared on write', with no dependence on the written value, and Table 2-9's prose says only 'Can be cleared only by the MVC instruction'. Under the legend's plain reading a write of 1 (or any write) should clear SAT; the emulator preserves it, and tests/cstub/c674x.c:2398-2403 encodes that as the expected value 0x14000300. The divergence is observable: a firmware read-modify-write of CSR to change GIE while SAT is set loses SAT under one reading and keeps it under the other. Not settleable from SPRUFE8B — see unresolved[].

verification.reasoning: Half of the precedence rule is implemented and half is missing, so fidelity cannot be strict and 'coverage is complete against the manual text' is wrong. What IS right: the one-delay-slot timing matches the printed-page-377 and printed-page-638 NOTE ('cannot be read in IFR until two cycles after the write') exactly — I traced the test and the queue (due = cycles+2); ISR-beats-ICR matches 'Any write to ICR is ignored by a simultaneous write to the same bit in ISR'; the 0xfff0 mask matches Figure 2-11's reserved 3-0. What is MISSING: the same two sentences also say (5.3.3, printed page 638) 'Incoming interrupts have priority and override any write to ICR' and (5.4.1, printed page 639) 'the automated write by the interrupt detection logic takes precedence and IFm remains set'. The retire code at cdj_c674x.c:2514 is `out.control[2] = ((out.control[2] & ~clears) | sets) & 0xfff2u` — `clears` is applied to a control[2] that already contains the incoming request, because the board loop calls cdj_c674x_interrupt before cdj_c674x_step (cdj2000_nxs_hpi.c:721-727, tools/cdj_dsp/replay.c:815). I wrote and ran scratchpad/verify_icr_race.c: with IF4 pre-set and an ICR clear of bit 4 in flight, raising INT4 on the cycle the clear retires leaves IFR == 0 — the request is silently DROPPED, no fault. The same precedence rule is stated for the device side in SPRUFK5A printed page 159 ('If a new event is received during the same cycle a clear is specified via an EVTCLRx register, the new event input takes precedence as an additional precaution against missing events') and is likewise absent from cdj_c6747_intc.c's EVTCLR handler.

verification.reasoning: This row is stronger than its 'approximation' grade suggests and everything in it checks out. Table 2-15 (printed page 45) says verbatim: 'If no interrupt is pending and enabled, HPEINT contains the value 0. The corresponding interrupt need not be enabled by NMIE (unless it is NMI) or by GIE.' The emulator's synthesis (cdj_c674x.c:188-196) ANDs IFR & IER & 0xfff2 and counts trailing zeros, which gets BOTH clauses right — it ignores GIE, returns 0 when nothing is pending, and because IER bit 1 is NMIE the 'unless it is NMI' exception falls out correctly. Write mask 0xfffffc00 is exactly Figure 2-12's R/W ISTB field (31-10) with HPEINT R-0 and bits 4-0 R-0. Scan order (lowest bit first) matches Table 5-1 (printed page 628: Reset > NMI > INT4 ... > INT15). The test (tests/cstub/c674x.c:2345-2356) asserts 0x008003ff -> 0x00800000 stored and a read of 0x00800080 with IFR/IER {4,7} — 4<<5 = 0x80, hand-derivable. The reset value is independently right: SPRUH91D HOST1CFG (printed page 180) gives DSP_ISTP_RST_VAL reset 1C00h in bits 31-10, i.e. 0x1C00 << 10 = 0x00700000.

verification.reasoning: Upheld, with a note on how thin the register half of the evidence is. Figure 2-10 (printed page 43) specifies only a 32-bit R/W field with an indeterminate reset value, so the cited round-trip loop (tests/cstub/c674x.c:2413-2424, writing 0x12345678+id) is trivially satisfiable by any storage and is weak 'reference-backed' evidence on its own. The load-bearing claim is the entry identity, and that IS independently supported: 5.4.4 (printed page 643) says 'The address of the first annulled execute packet (n + 5) is loaded in IRP', Figure 5-4 (printed page 641) puts n+5's E1 at cycle 6, and the entry tests assert control[6] == the pre-interrupt PC (0x1000/0x1040) and that it is not replaced by requests latched during the nine-cycle interval. I also found a manual rule that the emulator gets right and the track never mentions: 5.5.2 says that when an interrupt annuls any but the first cycle of a multicycle NOP or IDLE, 'the address of the next execute packet in the pipeline is saved in NRP or IRP. This prevents returning to an IDLE instruction or a multicycle NOP that was interrupted.' verification.reasoning: Two problems, one in the evidence description and one in coverage. (1) THE STATED RATIONALE FOR 0x7ff0 IS WRONG. tests/cstub/c6747-intc.c:25-26 reprograms INTMUX3 to 0x220e0d0c, putting INTSEL15 = 0x22 = 34, and only then (lines 70-77) writes EVTSET0 = all ones. That is why INT15 is missing from 0x7ff0. Under the genuine reset mux every one of INT4..INT15 selects an event in bank 0 and the answer would be 0xfff0. The expected value is still hand-derivable, but the row's explanation of what it establishes is incorrect. (2) THE OPEN QUESTION IS PARTLY ANSWERABLE, and it exposes a gap. SPRUFK5A printed page 159 states a primary-source precedence rule I could not find cited anywhere in the model: 'If a new event is received during the same cycle a clear is specified via an EVTCLRx register, the new event input takes precedence as an additional precaution against missing events.' cdj_c6747_intc_write_delivery's EVTCLR branch is a bare `s->event_flag[bank] &= ~(uint32_t)value` with no precedence handling, so the rule is unmodelled at the device level exactly as its CPU-side twin is unmodelled at :2514. That is the same defect class as IC-CR-ISR-ICR and is enough to make implementation partial. The generic selection logic itself is correct: request_selected_event reads the 7-bit INTSEL byte for each of CPUINT4..15, can map one event onto several interrupts, and can never produce a bit outside 4..15.

I read MpySpCase (c674x.c:861-879), the AddSp/SubSp form sweep (1277-1306) and the add_sub_sp_cases status table (1308-1340), and hand-verified expectations: 1.5*2 = 0x40400000; -2.5 * 8.6(0x4109999A) = -21.5 = 0xC1AC0000; (1+2^-23)^2 nearest = 0x3f800002 and upward = 0x3f800003; 8.6 + (-2.5) = 0x40C33334, which is the correct SP neighbour of 6.10000038 and not 0x40C33333 — precisely the kind of value that cannot be guessed or copied carelessly. Status words are manual-anchored: 0x0e0 = INFO|OVER|INEX and 0x0c0 = OVER|INEX for the overflow pair, 0x010 = INVAL alone for infinity*zero. I verified the RMODE encoding the whole rounding-mode dimension rests on against SPRUFE8B printed page 60 (PDF page 60), Table 2-25: 0 = nearest, 1h = toward 0, 2h = toward +infinity, 3h = toward -infinity — which matches the new test's modes[] = {FE_TONEAREST, FE_TOWARDZERO, FE_UPWARD, FE_DOWNWARD}, so that mapping is manual-derived, not emulator-derived, and the test is not circular. I rebuilt and reran the new test myself: cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror compiles with no diagnostics and it prints 'checked MPYSP=80000 ADDSP=80000 SUBSP=80000, failures=0'. I read its generator and confirmed the exponent bounds actually enforce the representability argument (MPYSP operands in [64,190]; ADDSP/SUBSP second operand constrained to within 25 exponents of the first), and that it skips non-normal results, so the double->float conversion really is a single correct SP rounding. verification.reasoning: All 14 rows confirmed dispatched, using the assembler as the oracle for the op-field encoding rather than trusting the source comments. Non-extended (bit 8 = 0): LDHU = 0x01900204 (op 0), LDBU = 0x...214 (1), LDB = 0x...224 (2), STB = 0x...234 (3), LDH = 0x...244 (4), STH = 0x...254 (5), LDW = 0x...264 (6), STW = 0x...274 (7) — all caught by (w & 0x10c) == 0x04 with the code's size table (op>=6 -> 4, op in {0,4,5} -> 2, else 1) and sign_extend on op 2 and 4 exactly right. Extended (bit 8 = 1): LDDW = 0x01100364 (op 6 -> pair, aligned, load), STDW = 0x01100344 (op 4 -> pair, aligned, store), LDNW = 0x01900334 (op 3 -> nonaligned word load), STNW = 0x01900354 (op 5), LDNDW = 0x01900324 (op 2 -> pair nonaligned load), STNDW = 0x01900374 (op 7) — matching the six guards 0x124/0x134/0x144/0x154/0x164/0x174. I also checked the LDNDW sc-bit handling: asm6x puts the pair number in bits 27-24 and sc in bit 23, so the code's dst = (w>>23)&31 followed by scale = (w & 1<<23) ? 8 : 1 and dst &= ~1u is a correct unification of the two fields, not a hack — for LDNDW *A4,A3:A2 = 0x01900324 the field reads 2 (A2) with sc = 0. The four approximations are genuine refusals (stop() calls), not invented behaviour, so fidelity=approximation is the honest label.

rows.exclusions_and_approximations: DECODER BUG. The second documented form, 'ADDAB/ADDAH/ADDAW (.unit) B14/B15, ucst15, dst', is rejected as 'reserved predicate'. SPRUFE8B printed page 115 (PDF page 115) gives its opcode as bits 31-28 = fixed 0001, dst 27-23, ucst15 22-8, y 7, bits 6-2 = 01111, s 1, p 0, and states verbatim 'This instruction is executed unconditionally, it cannot be predicated.' Those four bits are an opcode field, not creg/z. The probe word 0x1280043C decodes exactly as ADDAB .D1 B14, 4, A5 under that figure; cdj_c674x.c:1529-1531 computes creg=0, z=1 and rejects. TI deliberately places this form in the load/store format's reserved-predicate hole: had the check not fired, op=(w>>4)&7=3 with (w&0x0c)==12 would have executed it as STB with a 15-bit offset at cdj_c674x.c:1603. So the behaviour is fail-closed, but the instruction is unimplemented and the diagnostic is misleading. ADDAH uses the same second figure on printed page 120 and ADDAW on 123; ADDAD has no such form (printed pages 117-118), which is why the probe reports ADDAD as all-forms-accepted.

verification.reasoning: Confirmed independently and then strengthened. asm6x -mv6740 emits for ADDAB .D2 B14,4,A5 exactly 0x1280043C — the word the track names — plus ADDAH = 0x1280045C and ADDAW = 0x1280047C. For 0x1280043C, creg = w>>29 = 0 and z = (w>>28)&1 = 1, so cdj_c674x.c:1531 returns stop(..., 'reserved predicate') before any opcode classification. SPRUFE8B printed page 115 carries the second Opcode figure and the sentence 'executed unconditionally, it cannot be predicated' (build/references/sprufe8b.txt:5731), with the same sentence on pages 120 and 123 for ADDAH/ADDAW. The seven register/ucst5 forms are all correct — I decoded each assembler word and checked the code's arithmetic: ADDAB 0x32, ADDAH 0x36, ADDAW 0x3A, ADDAD 0x3D, SUBAB 0x33, SUBAH 0x37, SUBAW 0x3B, with scale = (op-0x30)/4 giving 0/1/2/3 and the immediate selector correctly switching to op&1 for ADDAD at 0x3c-0x3d. TWO ADDITIONS the track missed, both of which make the bug more damning. First, the same file already handles four other architecturally-unconditional forms ahead of the creg test: CALLP at cdj_c674x.c:1164 matches (w & 0xf000007c) == 0x10000010 — the identical fixed bits-31-28 = 0001 pattern — and DINT/RINT (~1505-1528) and SPMASK (1060-1064) likewise 'continue' before line 1531. So the ordering requirement is understood and was applied three times; ADDAx is a plain omission, not an unknown hazard. Second, I enumerated the complete unconditional set from the manual (13 'cannot be predicated' hits): ADDAB/ADDAH/ADDAW long-immediate (pp 115/120/123), MPY2IR (367), RINT (413), RPACK2 (416), SADDSUB (427), SADDSUB2 (429), SHFL3 (445), SMPY32 (470), SPKERNELR (483), SPMASK (487), SPMASKR (489). Every one except the three ADDAx forms is either already handled before the predicate test or unimplemented anyway, so the defect is bounded at exactly three instructions today — but MPY2IR and SMPY32 would hit the same trap the moment they are added.

(1) Figure E-5 M3, SPRUFE8B printed page 744 (PDF page 744): bits 4-1 = 1111 and bit 0 = s, so the pattern is (w & 0x1e) == 0x1e; grep for '& 0x1e' across cdj_c674x.c finds it ONLY at line 707 inside instruction_unit, returning 64u << side (the .M unit), and nowhere in the execute dispatch — so the format is classified and never executed, exactly as claimed. The figure's mnemonic table confirms the eight instructions (MPY/MPYH/MPYLH/MPYHL at SAT=0, SMPY/SMPYH/SMPYLH/SMPYHL at SAT=1). The track cited line 686 for this; the actual line is 707. (2) Figure F-29 Sx2op, printed page 755: the figure's fixed bits (bit10=0, bit6=0, bit5=1, bit4=0, bits3-1=111) give mask 0x47e and pattern 0x02e exactly as claimed, and that pattern appears only in instruction_unit at cdj_c674x.c:707 ((w & 0x047e) == 0x2e -> 4u << side), never in execute. CORRECTION to the track: it says Sx2op and Sx5 'differ only in bits 10 and 6', but Figures F-29 and F-30 both show bit 6 = 0; they differ only in bit 10. (3) Figure F-32 Sx1b, printed page 756: the figure gives N3 at 15-13, bits 12-11 = 00, src2 at 10-7 (4 bits), bits 6-1 = 110111, bit 0 = s, with NOTE 'src2 from B0-B15' — so s is a free unit selector and s=0 is legal. cdj_c674x.c:1355 requires (w & 0x187f) == 0x006f, i.e. bit 0 = 1, rejecting all 128 s=0 words, while the operand path cpu->r[1][(w>>7)&15] is already correct for both units. WHY I DOWNGRADE VALIDATION: the probe that produced 53,856 / 11,440 / 176 / 64 was a scratch artefact; it is not in the repository, there is no manifest, gate or hash recording it, and analysis/dsp/ plus tools/cdj_dsp/isa_probe.py and tests/cstub/c674x-isa-probe.c are all untracked in git. verification.reasoning: The creg/z decode itself is correct — cdj_c674x.c:1531-1535 uses bank[] = {0,1,1,1,0,0,0} and index[] = {0,0,1,2,1,2,0}, giving 001->B0, 010->B1, 011->B2, 100->A1, 101->A2, 110->A0, with creg==7 and (creg==0 && z) rejected, which is an exact match to SPRUFE8B Table 3-9 (printed page 77), and the '^ z' polarity is right. The false-predicate tests at tests/cstub/c674x.c:965-977 and 1024-1029 genuinely reach predicate-body behaviour (they assert no delayed result and no FADCR warning, not merely a fetch), so validation=reference-backed-tests holds. But implementation=supported does not, and the row's own sentence 'Coverage gap in testing, not implementation' is contradicted by the track's own ISA-ADDR finding. The predicate test is evaluated at cdj_c674x.c:1531 BEFORE opcode classification, and that placement is precisely why three architecturally-unconditional instructions — ADDAB/ADDAH/ADDAW in their B14/B15 + ucst15 form, whose bits 31-28 are a fixed opcode field 0001, not creg/z — are unreachable and misdiagnosed. That is a defect in how predication is implemented, not a gap in how it is tested. The same file proves the point: CALLP (cdj_c674x.c:1164, matching the identical 0x1000xxxx fixed-opcode pattern), DINT/RINT (~1505-1528) and SPMASK (1060-1064) are all dispatched ahead of line 1531 precisely because they are unconditional. The architecture therefore requires opcode classification before the predicate test for a known, enumerable set of formats, and the core does this for four of them and not for three others. implementation -> partial. Residual exposure: MPY2IR (printed page 367) and SMPY32 (printed page 470) are also unconditional and would hit the same trap if implemented.

(1) c674x-circular.c:107-153 (aligned_memory) NEVER attempts a misaligned aligned-form access. I traced every address it can produce: base is 0x1100 or 0x1118, offset is (9 or 33) * size, and wrap() masks 5 or 6 low bits — all three are multiples of 8, so every generated address is naturally aligned for every form in the table. The test cannot reject anything, and there is no rejection assertion in that function. (2) c674x.c:1676-1700 is the compact Doff4DW/STDW decode matrix, not an alignment test. The genuine evidence, uncited, is tests/cstub/c674x.c:1824-1826: an LDH with r[0][10]=0x10c1 is rejected with `!c.load_count` and the pointer unchanged. That is halfword only. I could not find any assertion that a WORD (LDW/STW at a non-word boundary) or DOUBLEWORD (LDDW/STDW at a non-8 boundary) aligned-form access is rejected for the 32-bit forms; the only doubleword-alignment rejection I found is the compact Dstk case at c674x.c:~1470. So the row's 'halfword/word/doubleword' requirement is validated for one of three sizes. Verdict downgraded on evidence scope and citations even though the final label survives for the halfword case.

verification.reasoning: Implementation verified and correct: cdj_c674x.c:1686-1703 uses `(op >= 0x3c ? op & 1 : op & 2)` for immediate-vs-register and `(op - 0x30) / 4` for the x1/x2/x4/x8 shift, with subtract only for op < 0x3c && (op & 1), so there is indeed no SUBAD. Validation is circular in two layers. The arithmetic() sweep computes its expected value as `bool immediate = op >= 0x3c ? op & 1 : op & 2; uint32_t delta = (immediate ? field : offsets[k]) << ((op - 0x30) / 4); uint32_t linear = op < 0x3c && (op & 1) ? bases[j] - delta : bases[j] + delta; assert(c.r[side][10] == wrap(bases[j], linear, bk))` — the opfield decomposition, the shift formula AND the wrap rule are all duplicated from the implementation. The sweep is large (5 bases x 6 offsets x 32 block sizes x 14 ops x 4 registers x 2 banks) but every one of those cases is checked against a re-implementation, so the breadth buys robustness against typos, not against a wrong reading of the manual. Example 3-5 again lives only in a scratchpad probe. Note also the row's own next_acceptance_test admits the non-existent SUBAD encoding (op 0x3E/0x3F) is not negatively tested.

verification.reasoning: Two corrections. (1) fidelity=strict is incoherent for implementation=unsupported: there is no modelled behaviour for fidelity to be strict about. Per the track's own evidence model the value must be unknown. Choosing to fault rather than fake the stall is good engineering, but it is not architectural fidelity. (2) The 'neither wider nor narrower' claim is WRONG, and demonstrably so from the source. The interlock check at cdj_c674x.c:1635-1637 sits OUTSIDE `if (enabled)`: `if (b >= 4 && b <= 7 && cpu->control_ready[0] > cpu->cycles) return stop(...)`. So a PREDICATED-OFF LD/ST in the packet after an MVC-to-AMR also faults, even though a predicated-off instruction performs no addressing and the manual's rule ('if the LD, ST, ADDA, or SUBA instruction uses the A4-A7 or B4-B7 registers for addressing') has no analogue for it. The refusal window is therefore WIDER than the manual's scope along the predication axis, and that case is untested — mvc_and_reserved's nop loop uses an unpredicated ADDA only. I verified the manual text verbatim: SPRUFE8B 3.8.9, printed page 82, is exactly as the row quotes it. The fail-closed behaviour for the unpredicated case is genuinely and independently tested (assert(ok == (bool)nop)), so validation survives for that case.

verification.reasoning: I answered the open question and it breaks the row. Termination during loading is not exotic, it is trivial and legal. Probe: `[B1] SPLOOPW 1` with B1 == 0 and a 12-cycle body stops after 5 steps with "SPLOOPW termination during loading not implemented", while still unsealed. With ii = 1 every cycle is a stage boundary, so for any SPLOOPW whose dynlen exceeds 4 and whose condition is false early, a boundary termination DURING loading is unavoidable. 7.10.3 printed page 691 explicitly contemplates it: "If the termination condition is determined in the last loading stage, the dynlen must be a multiple of ii" — a rule that only exists because the condition can be determined while loading. So 7.10.2's stage-boundary termination is implemented only for the sealed phase: implementation is partial and fidelity is approximation, not strict. Separately, and worth recording because it is the one place I expected to find a bug and did not: the TERMINATION POLARITY is CORRECT. The SPLOOPW instruction page printed page 486 says "The termination condition is the value of the predicate register selected by the creg and z fields", which read literally inverts the core's behaviour; but 7.10.2 printed page 691 is precise — "The stage boundary termination condition is true when a stage boundary is reached and the SPLOOPW instruction condition operand evaluates as FALSE 3 cycles before the stage boundary" — and Example 7-12 printed page 691 confirms it (`[!A1] SPLOOPW`, `CMPLT B4,0,A1`, comment "term_cond = !A1"). The core stores the predicate value and terminates on `!(loop_pred_history & 4)`, i.e. on the predicate being false three cycles earlier. I verified the z-bit sense against TI (`[A1] ADD` -> 0x81882078 bit28=0; `[!A1] ADD` -> 0x91882078 bit28=1), so `condition = (r != 0) ^ invert` is the predicate expression and the core matches 7.10.2 exactly. 7.10.1's "initial termination condition is always false" is also correctly implemented via `loop_pred_history = 7` plus `cycle >= 4`.

Full-width: printed page 487 places bit25=M2, 24=M1, 23=D2, 22=D1, 21=S2, 20=S1, 19=L2, 18=L1; `*mask = (w >> 18) & 255` with the documented order L1,L2,S1,S2,D1,D2,M1,M2 matches exactly, and instruction_unit's 1<<side / 4<<side / 16<<side / 64<<side for L/S/D/M is consistent with it. Execute a PM instruction, if present, with no effect on the buffer contents" and "If an SPMASK instruction is encountered when the loop buffer is idle ... executes as a NOP") are quoted accurately. verification.reasoning: The conditions the row lists ARE in the code and I checked each against 7.13.1 printed page 697 — `boundary_cycle % ii == 0` with sealed, `terminating`, `opening < 4`, the armed/draining guard, and `control[13] >= loading_stages` where loading_stages = ceil(length/ii), which is the manual's ceil(dynlen/ii) and its own gloss "equal to the number of loading stages". But the row's enumeration silently drops the FIRST condition in the manual's list: "An enabled interrupt is pending and not architecturally blocked (for example, in branch delay slots)." That condition is only partly implemented — cdj_c674x.c:880 defers on taken branches only (see PKT-BRDELAY), so an interrupt presented inside an untaken branch's delay slots while a loop is active can be armed when hardware would block it. The row lists the branch-delay issue under PKT-BRDELAY but presents the 7.13.1 list here as complete. Two further evidence gaps: the ILC boundary condition itself is never pinned — the row's own next_acceptance_test asks for `ILC == ceil(dynlen/ii) - 1` and no such case exists, so the condition is only exercised on the happy path where it passes; and the "interrupts are automatically disabled 2 cycles before an SPLOOP(D/W)" rule is subsumed into the four-cycle opening, which the row calls defensible but which is over-conservative in one direction (the manual's four-cycle opening is worded for SPLOOPD/SPLOOPW specifically) and unmodelled in the other (nothing blocks an interrupt in the two cycles BEFORE the setup packet).

verification.reasoning: The validation label does not survive reading the tests. 7.13.2 printed page 698 lists five exceptions. Items 2 and 3 (the SPMASK reversal) are strict-mode fail-closed, which the row admits. The problem is items 1, 4 and 5: the tests the row cites for them — tests/cstub/c674x.c:2498-2524 (B IRP resume, SPLOOPD executing as SPLOOP, parallel setup op suppressed) and :2529-2568 (BNOP label,n as NOP n+1) — run inside a `cdj_c674x_loop_set_functional_timing(true)` region and the mode is only restored at :2618 (`cdj_c674x_loop_set_functional_timing(false)`). Functional timing is opt-in, is not the shipped default, and by the module's own header comment adds two epilog cycles to delayed-count loops. So three of the five 7.13.2 items are validated only in a non-default configuration, and the row labels the evidence "independent-of-emulator" without saying so. Strict-mode resume is covered only by the fail-closed cases (:2570-2578 "SPLOOP interrupt-return buffer unavailable") and by the full SPLOOP/SPLOOPW resume at :2798-2844. Also, the row says BNOP label,n -> NOP n+1 is "implemented for immediate forms only, with register branches left under the fail-closed control-instruction check" — that understates a related asymmetry: a BNOP in a NON-returning body is rejected outright even though 3.8.11.1 printed page 82 permits it (see LOOP-SETUP), so the only body in which BNOP works at all is a returning one.

rows.exclusions_and_approximations: This is the loop-specific consequence of PKT-UNIT: because functional-unit occupancy is never compared anywhere, the architectural exception TI designed precisely to catch an unmasked program-memory/buffer conflict can never fire. Only the eight-operation capacity limit is enforced. Likewise IERR.LBX/MSX do not exist, so the missed-stall exception of 7.15.2 is unmodelled - consistent with there being no cross-path stall model at all (PKT-STALL). 7.16 and 7.17 are assembler-enforced restrictions and are correctly not the core's responsibility, but 7.15.2 explicitly says the assembler cannot prevent every case and the internal exception is the backstop.

rows.requirement: A hardware exception occurs on an unmasked resource conflict between a program-memory instruction and a loop-buffer instruction, or between draining and reloading buffer instructions; an internal exception setting IERR.LBX and IERR.MSX occurs when a stall required for correctness was skipped because the instruction came from the loop buffer

rows.exclusions_and_approximations: The core has cdj_c674x_interrupt for maskable CPU interrupts INT4..15 only. There is no EXCEP/NMI entry, no NRP or NTSR handling beyond control-register storage, and no IERR. So the exception-during-loop behaviour - which differs sharply from the interrupt case in that it does NOT drain an epilog - has no implementation to assess and nothing to test against. Noted here because it is the one 7.13.x subsection with no counterpart in the core, and because it interacts with LOOP-RESCONF: the exceptions 7.15.1/7.15.2 require would be delivered through exactly this missing path.
rows.implementation_location: none - no exception delivery path exists in emulator/qemu/cdj_c674x.c
rows.manual_section: 7.13.3 Exceptions
rows.next_acceptance_test: Out of scope until an exception delivery path exists. When one is added, the first loop test should be that an exception during an active loop idles the buffer on the same cycle with no epilog and sets NTSR.SPLX.
rows.open_questions: Whether any exception source in the modelled C6747 peripheral set can fire during DSP execution, which would determine the priority of this gap. That is a peripheral-track question.
rows.requirement: If an internal or external exception occurs while the loop buffer is active: the exception is recognized immediately, the buffer becomes idle, NO epilog is executed, and TSR is copied to NTSR with SPLX=1 in NTSR and 0 in TSR

verification.reasoning: No verifier entry for this row.
